## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammadevaputtacariya* (Cp 18, also titled *Dhammādhamma-Devaputta-Cariya*) is a short poetic narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [Bareau; SuttaCentral]. The text recounts a past life in which the Bodhisatta was reborn as a deity of great psychic power and authority named Dhamma, who was moved by deep compassion for the beings of all worlds [Bareau; SuttaCentral].

No early cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are recorded for this text on SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus with a score of 10 or higher [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. Internal text reuse is identified by DharmaNexus exclusively with the text's traditional Pali commentary, the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares seven matching segments (532 characters in total), the longest alignment running between segments 4.2–5.4 of the base text and paragraphs 1144–1147 of the commentary [DharmaNexus].

In modern scholarship, the Pali verses were edited, translated into French, and compared with their corresponding Jātaka material by André Bareau [Bareau]. On SuttaCentral, translations into three languages are indexed, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *The Conduct of the Deity Named Dhamma* [SuttaCentral].
